documents.title: Small molecule structure elucidation from NMR spectra with generative and reasoning models.
documents.abstract: Elucidating the structures of unknown small molecules remains a major challenge in chemistry, pharmacology, and drug discovery. While nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is the gold standard for structure elucidation, interpreting spectra remains labor-intensive and requires expert knowledge to navigate the vast space of possible structures. Here, we present an AI system for rapid, automated de novo structure elucidation that combines a molecular generative model with a scientific reasoning agent. Its generative component, ChefNMR2, is an atomic flow-matching model that predicts smal
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: MultiTargetDB: a comprehensive database of multitarget ligands for polypharmacology research and drug discovery.
documents.abstract: Multitarget drug discovery has gained considerable traction in recent years, particularly for the treatment of complex diseases. Despite the growing demand for dedicated, well-curated resources to advance polypharmacology research and rational multitarget drug discovery, such resources remain severely limited. Here, we present MultiTargetDB, a database of multitarget ligands integrated with comprehensive biological annotations and measurement-level provenance. At the small molecule level, MultiTargetDB integrates chemical structures (including molecular scaffolds), their drug development stage

documents.title: Computational network pharmacology and molecular simulations to explore the potential mechanisms of Pyrrosia piloselloides compounds against prostate cancer.
documents.abstract: Prostate cancer is major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality in men worldwide. Emerging evidence highlights the dragon scale fern (Pyrrosia piloselloides or P. piloselloides) has demonstrated anticancer potential, but its molecular mechanisms against prostate cancer remain unclear. The study aimed to investigate its potential anticancer compounds and underlying molecular mechanisms using an integrated in silico approach.
documents.journal: Journal of the Egyptian National Cancer Institute

documents.title: From LC-MS Metabolomic Profiling to AIEnabled Navigation of NPs Chemical Space: Recent Advances and Emerging Directions.
documents.abstract: Natural products (NPs) occupy a unique region of chemical space and continue to provide privileged scaffolds for drug discovery, chemical ecology, and biotechnology. However, the exploration of NP diversity remains constrained by the complexity of biological extracts, the low annotation rate of LC-MS features, and the rediscovery of known metabolites. Recent advances in LC-HRMS/MS-based metabolomics, coupled with expanding spectral and structural databases, molecular networking, and in silico annotation methods, have considerably improved the characterization of complex metabolomes and facilit

documents.title: Modeling ethnic differences via drug-predicted clearance from chemical structures.
documents.abstract: Ethnic differences in pharmacokinetics can result in clinically relevant differences in drug efficacy and safety, even when identical doses are administered. Although mechanistic approaches such as physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling can be used to evaluate population-specific pharmacokinetics, there remains a need for complementary screening approaches that can assess ethnic difference risk at very early stages of drug discovery with limited experimental information. The aim of this study was to develop a machine-learning-based approach to assess the risk of ethnic differences in o
documents.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences

documents.title: Structure-function relationships in a square-planar Cu(ii) hybrid halometalate: experimental, DFT, molecular docking, optical, and biological studies.
documents.abstract: A novel organic-inorganic copper(ii) hybrid halometalate, (C6H8BrN2)2[CuBr4], was successfully synthesized and investigated using complementary experimental and computational approaches. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis revealed discrete square-planar [CuBr4]2- anions embedded within a three-dimensional supramolecular architecture stabilized by N-H⋯Br hydrogen bonds, π-π stacking interactions, and halogen contacts. Optical studies indicated semiconducting characteristics with an estimated band gap of approximately 2.5 eV, together with a broad visible emission assigned to ligand-to-me

documents.title: In Silico Investigation of Candidate Anticancer Targets for Aryltetralin Lignans Previously Reported from Cleistanthus Species.
documents.abstract: Aryltetralin lignans isolated from the fruits of Cleistanthus species exhibit substantial cytotoxic activity, although the molecular interactions underlying these effects remain incompletely understood. This study combined computational target investigation with previously published experimental chemical characterization and cytotoxic evidence and no new isolation or cytotoxicity experiments were carried out. Cleistantoxin, 7-hydroxypicropolygamain, neo-cleistantoxin, cleisindoside A, cleisindoside D, and cleistonkinin D were previously isolated from C. indochinensis, C. tonkinensis, C. eberha

documents.title: Integrating Multisource Target Evidence with Machine-Learning Potency Prediction for Alzheimer's Disease Drug Discovery.
documents.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) target evidence is distributed across biological, chemical, structural, regulatory, and trial-registry sources, complicating reproducible target evaluation and modeling. We developed a traceable data-to-model platform that integrates AGORA-centered evidence through Target Explorer, Drug-Target Lookup, and Model Portfolio workspaces. The resource contains 967 targets, 452,249 compounds, and 1,430,260 measurements. On a curated PIK3CA dataset, target-specific fine-tuning of the Boltz-2 affinity head increased Pearson r from 0.248 to 0.560 and reduced mean absolute error
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Advancing CD38 from a marker of disease activity to an active regulator of interferon responses in juvenile dermatomyositis.
documents.abstract: Juvenile dermatomyositis (JDM), the most common pediatric inflammatory myopathy, is driven by an overactive immune signaling pathway called type I interferon. Current treatment relies on broadly immunosuppressive agents that lack mechanistic specificity, often fail to achieve durable disease control, and can result in off-target toxicity and irreversible disease-related damage in many patients. CD38, a nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+)-consuming ectoenzyme with known roles in immune cell metabolism, is elevated in JDM, but whether CD38 marks disease activity or plays a causal role in di
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Computational Identification of GABA-A Receptor Ligands Targeting the Histamine Allosteric Pocket.
documents.abstract: The γ-aminobutyric acid type A (GABA-A) receptor is a key regulator of inhibitory neurotransmission in the central nervous system, and a promising target for cognitive and neurological disorders. Histamine interacts with a distinct allosteric pocket located at the β3-β3 subunit interface, providing an opportunity for the discovery of novel ligands. In the present study, an integrated in silico workflow combining ligand-based similarity analysis, ADMET filtering, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations was applied to identify candidate ligands for this histamine-associated site. D

documents.title: Navigating the Eukaryotic Paradox: Insights for AI-Driven Computational Strategies Against Antifungal Resistance.
documents.abstract: The escalating crisis of invasive fungal infections and increasing antifungal resistance demand rapid therapeutic innovation. Given the critically narrow clinical arsenal, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have emerged as pivotal strategies to accelerate drug repurposing, providing a rapid alternative to de novo drug discovery. However, translational success in medical mycology faces a major biological hurdle: the "eukaryotic paradox," the extensive genomic, metabolic, and structural homology between fungal cells and human hosts. This review provides a critical and compara

documents.title: Network-enabled drug repurposing identifies lithium to promote cardiomyocyte proliferation.
documents.abstract: The adult mammalian heart has minimal regenerative capacity, limited in part by endogenous cardiomyocyte (CM) renewal. Although CM proliferation is a promising target in both congenital and adult heart disease, no current therapies specifically target this process. Progress has been hindered by the complexity of CM proliferation signaling networks, which may require systems-level approaches. The overall goal of this study was to leverage systems modeling to identify FDA approved drugs that have the potential to be repurposed towards CM proliferation. To achieve this goal, we developed a comput
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: QSAR-Guided In Silico Design of Piperazinylanthranilamide Factor Xa Inhibitors: Applicability-Domain Assessment, ADMET Profiling, Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics, and MM/GBSA.
documents.abstract: An integrated computational workflow was developed to prioritize piperazinylanthranilamide factor Xa (FXa) inhibitor candidates. Twenty literature compounds were geometry-optimized and described using alvaDesc to construct a constrained additive multivariate adaptive regression splines model. Internal validation and an assessment of the applicability domain guided the evaluation of 20 prospective analogs. Ten selected analogs and two same-series references were docked to FXa, with apixaban as the crystallographic comparator. Thirteen initial 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations were supplemen

documents.title: Donor-Resolved Analysis of HES1-Associated Fibroblast States in Systemic Sclerosis.
documents.abstract: Background/Objectives: We examined HES1-associated fibroblast states in systemic sclerosis (SSc) and the rationale for testing upstream γ-secretase inhibition with nirogacestat. Methods: We analysed 325,636 skin cells from 230 donors across five non-redundant cohorts using complete computational transcription-factor screens, donor-level activity and trajectory analyses, multiome data and spatial assays. Donors or independent simulations were the inference units, with cohort adjustment and multiplicity correction where applicable. Three independent 200 ns molecular dynamics runs per condition c

documents.title: Network Pharmacology of Natural Products from Computational Prediction to Experimental Validation.
documents.abstract: Natural products are important sources of bioactive compounds, but their complex chemical composition and multi-target effects make their mechanisms difficult to investigate using conventional approaches. Network pharmacology provides a systems-level framework for integrating chemical, biological, and disease-related information to investigate these complex interactions. This review describes the network pharmacology workflow, from active-compound screening, ADMET evaluation and target prediction to network construction and pathway enrichment, and the complementary roles of molecular docking a

documents.title: Machine Learning-Guided Virtual Screening Identifies a Novel MELK-Targeted Antiproliferative Lead Compound with G2/M Arrest Activity in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer and Lung Adenocarcinoma Cells.
documents.abstract: Background: Maternal embryonic leucine zipper kinase (MELK) is a cell cycle-regulated serine/threonine kinase frequently overexpressed in human malignancies, and represents a promising anticancer drug target. Discovery of structurally novel, highly selective MELK inhibitors remains an unmet need. Methods: In the study, we implemented an integrated computational pipeline combining four machine learning regressors (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, LightGBM), hierarchical Glide docking (HTVS to SP to XP), MM/GBSA rescoring, ADMET prediction, and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations to

documents.title: In Silico Discovery of a Potential PI3Kα Inhibitor Incorporating an Imidazole Moiety for Breast Cancer Treatment.
documents.abstract: Excessive activation of PI3Kα is prevalent in breast cancer, aberrantly activating the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway to drive tumor progression, thus rendering PI3Kα a vital therapeutic target. Two PI3Kα inhibitors (alpelisib and inavolisib) have been approved for clinical application. Inavolisib exerts a mutation-selective degradation mechanism and functions by directly eliminating aberrant proteins. To develop novel PI3Kα inhibitors, we employed multiple computational strategies including scaffold hopping based on the structure of inavolisib, -CDOCKER docking, Lipinski's rule of five, ADMET predicti

documents.title: Molecular Dynamics-Guided Triage of Approved Drugs Against Escherichia coli Resistance Targets Nominates Capmatinib, Metergoline and Nilotinib as Candidates for Experimental Testing.
documents.abstract: Virtual screening ranks compounds by scoring functions that correlate with molecular size, and hit lists are rarely benchmarked against compounds of established activity. We screened 2070 approved drugs against four Escherichia coli targets selected by pocket-druggability triage (FabI, LpxC, DHFR and GyrB), with each docking protocol validated by redocking its native ligand (RMSD 0.50-0.69 Å). Per target, the two top-scoring compounds and a reference inhibitor were simulated for 100 ns in triplicate (12 complexes, 3.6 μs). Docking did not recover the references: trimethoprim ranked 762/2068 an

documents.title: GPCRAgent: an intelligent multi-agent platform integrating knowledge graphs and large language models for GPCR-targeted drug discovery.
documents.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are major therapeutic targets in drug discovery. However, systematic characterization of GPCR functions and ligand interactions remains constrained by the high cost and complexity of experimental approaches. Although large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance in biomedical question answering, their direct application to GPCR research is limited by insufficient integration of structured domain knowledge and poor interpretability of generated inferences.

documents.title: Anticancer activity of sodium propionate in hepatocellular carcinoma cells via downregulation of HDAC2 and HDAC6.
documents.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is an aggressive malignancy driven by epigenetic dysregulation. This study investigates the anticancer potential of sodium propionate (SP) as an epigenetic modulator targeting histone deacetylases (HDACs) using an integrated in silico and in vitro approach. Bioinformatics analyses were conducted using publicly available HCC transcriptomic datasets from GEO database, disease gene database (GeneCards database), and chemical-gene interaction networks (Comparative Toxicogenomic Database) to identify potential therapeutic targets, HDAC2 and HDAC6 as key therapeutic ta

documents.title: Strengthening Japan's drug discovery and medical research ecosystem: AMED's innovation challenge.
documents.abstract: Japan continues to face challenges in translating life science and medical research into innovative medicines and healthcare technologies. The Japan Agency for Medical Research and Development (AMED), established in 2015, plays a central role in bridging basic research and practical application. To address gaps between research and development stages and to promote practical application of promising technological seeds from academia, AMED adopted five strategic priorities under its Third Mid- to Long-Term Plan (2025-2029). (1) Strengthen coordination across AMED programs to ensure seamless sup

documents.title: An educational activity tailored for undergraduate students on AI-driven nanobody design for targeted antiviral therapeutics.
documents.abstract: Protein-based biologics are converging at an unprecedented pace as generative artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes early-stage drug discovery. Nanobodies, single-domain antibody fragments derived from camelid heavy chain-only immunoglobulins, are an emerging class of antiviral biologics prized for their small size, stability, and access to cryptic viral epitopes. Traditional nanobody discovery relies on animal immunization and phage display screening, a process that can take 6 to 12 months and is entirely inaccessible within a standard undergraduate laboratory session. Here, we describe a suc

documents.title: Discovery of potential ALK inhibitors from Glycosmis phytochemicals via integrated machine learning and umbrella sampling approaches.
documents.abstract: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) is a key therapeutic target for various cancers because of its central role in tumor growth and survival signaling. This study employed an integrated computational workflow combining machine learning (ML), molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, umbrella sampling (US), and toxicity prediction to identify potential ALK inhibitors from 307 phytochemicals of the Glycosmis genus. A previously validated CatBoost regression model predicted binding free energies, leading to the selection of 26 compounds with ΔG ML < -11 kcal mol-1. Molecular docking id

documents.title: Design, synthesis, and docking analysis of benzene sulfonamide-[1,4]benzoxazepine hybrids as acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase inhibitors.
documents.abstract: A series of novel hybrid [1,4]benzoxazepine-based sulfonamide derivatives 9-12a-j were synthesized and evaluated for their inhibitory activity against acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE). Compounds 9a and 9b exhibited potent dual cholinesterase inhibition, with IC50 values of 9.04 and 8.61 µM against AChE and 3.08 and 4.64 µM against BChE, respectively. Compound 12j emerged as the most potent BChE inhibitor of the series (IC50 = 1.06 ± 0.11 µM), displaying pronounced BChE preference (SI = 10.37), whereas 9d showed the highest BChE selectivity (BChE IC50 = 4.18 ± 0.56 µ

documents.title: Innovative design and development of novel thiazole-paracetamol hybrids as COX inhibitors and immunomodulatory activity: design, synthesis, SAR, in vitro biological evaluation, and molecular docking analysis.
documents.abstract: The hybridization approach was employed to design a single pharmacophore based on the conjugation of paracetamol with thiazole derivatives, yielding thiazole-paracetamol hybrid derivatives 4-11 that utilize a linker from hydrazone (-C[double bond, length as m-dash]N-NH) and azo (-N[double bond, length as m-dash]N-) linkers, serving as the hydrogen bond donor/acceptor binding site. The structure of the designed derivatives was fully characterized and confirmed using analytical data (IR, 1H NMR, and 13C NMR), and elemental analysis. The anti-inflammatory potential of the synthesized hybrids was

documents.title: Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability Prediction by Integrating Deep Learning Representations with Chemical Compound Knowledge.
documents.abstract: Predicting blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability is essential for central nervous system drug discovery, but traditional descriptor-based methods of predicting BBB permeability lack structural context, and deep learning-based methods struggle with overfitting. We introduce a multimodel framework that integrates both transformer-derived molecular embeddings with physicochemical descriptors using a late-stage ensemble fusion strategy. Trained on both the B3DB and NeuTox data sets and evaluated on the benchmark BBBP, our model showed strong predictive performance, with data set-dependent perform

documents.title: Design, click synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel uracil-1,2,3-triazole hybrids as dual EGFR/CDK1 inhibitors: antiproliferative activity, mechanistic insights, and in silico studies.
documents.abstract: A novel series of uracil-1,2,3-triazole hybrids was designed, synthesized, and evaluated as dual EGFR/CDK1 inhibitors to target cancer cell proliferation and survival. Synthesis was initiated via the nucleophilic substitution of 2-chloro-N-(1,3-dimethyl-2,6-dioxo-pyrimidin-4-yl)acetamide (3) with sodium azide, yielding the key intermediate 4. Subsequent copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloadditions (CuAAC) with various terminal alkynes and 1,3-dicarbonyls afforded the target triazole analogues 6a,b, 8a-c, and 10b,c. In vitro antiproliferative screening against a panel of four human cancer cell

documents.title: Conversational Multi-Agentic Network-Driven Disease Module Identification and Drug Repurposing Prediction With ChatDRex: Platform Development Study.
documents.abstract: Repurposing approved drugs offers a time- and cost-effective alternative to traditional drug development. However, in silico prediction of repurposing candidates is challenging and requires the effective collaboration of specialists in various fields, including pharmacology, medicine, biology, and bioinformatics. Fragmented, specialized algorithms and tools often address only narrow aspects of the overall problem. Heterogeneous, unstructured data landscapes require the expertise of specialized users. Hence, diverse data sources might not integrate smoothly across workflows.

documents.title: Machine learning for RNA-small molecule interactions: methodologies, evaluation, and future directions.
documents.abstract: RNA is emerging as a compelling therapeutic target due to its rich structural diversity and central involvement in gene regulation, splicing, translation, and cellular signaling. Alongside advances in structural biology, computational approaches, especially machine learning and deep learning, have transformed the systematic analysis of RNA-small molecule interactions. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive survey of computational methods for RNA-small molecule interaction prediction, with a particular emphasis on three core tasks: binding site prediction, binding preference prediction, and

documents.title: ADMET property prediction and toxicity profiling of CDK2 inhibitors: a practical cheminformatics tutorial using ADMET-AI 2.0 and RDKit.
documents.abstract: Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity (ADMET) prediction plays a central role in modern computer-aided drug discovery by enabling early evaluation of pharmacokinetic behaviour and safety liabilities. This tutorial presents a reproducible computational workflow for large-scale ADMET profiling using ADMET-AI 2.0, a graph neural network-based prediction platform, applied to 200 cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2) inhibitors curated from ChEMBL release 35. Implemented within an annotated Jupyter notebook, the workflow integrates cheminformatics preprocessing, physicochemical p

documents.title: Can AI Help Repurpose Drugs to Fight Against Antibiotic Resistance?
documents.abstract: Drug repurposing and development to meet the threat of antimicrobial resistance can be costly and time-consuming, but AI models may be able to help. In this News and Perspectives article, JMIR Correspondent Sara Novak reports on recent research training models to identify candidate drugs to treat resistant infections.

documents.title: Integrated experimental and computational study of a novel indenonaphthodiazepine[5.3.3]propellane as a potential inhibitor of Mcl-1.
documents.abstract: Myeloid cell leukemia-1 (Mcl-1) is a key anti-apoptotic protein that drives resistance to chemotherapy, making it a critical oncology target. In this study, we synthesized a new indenonaphthodiazepine[5.3.3]propellane via a one-pot multicomponent reaction and characterized its structure by FT-IR, 1H-NMR, 13C-NMR, and mass spectrometry. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations at the B3LYP/6-31G (d) level were carried out to study its electronic features and reactive centers. In molecular docking against Mcl-1, the propellane derivative showed a binding score of -5.678 kcal mol-1, outperfor

documents.title: Utilising digital technologies for mycetoma management: A comprehensive review of advances and opportunities.
documents.abstract: Mycetoma is a neglected tropical disease characterised by chronic, destructive infections of subcutaneous tissues, predominantly affecting populations in endemic regions with limited healthcare resources. Delayed diagnosis, limited treatment options, and restricted access to specialised healthcare contribute to substantial morbidity, disability, and socioeconomic burden. Digital technologies offer promising opportunities to address these challenges and improve mycetoma care. Artificial intelligence (AI) can support early detection and diagnostic accuracy through the analysis of clinical images

documents.title: Machine Learning-Guided Discovery of Novel Inhibitors of Escherichia coli MurB.
documents.abstract: MurB, a key enzyme involved in bacterial cell wall biosynthesis, represents a promising target for antibacterial drug discovery. In this study, a machine learning assay was employed to identify potential inhibitors targeting E. coli MurB. Five machine learning models were constructed using AutoMolDesigner, of which the RDKit_2D-based Model_2 was selected as the optimal activity-prediction model for virtual screening of an in-house compound library, yielding 238 compounds. These compounds were subsequently subjected to FRED molecular docking, and 16 candidate compounds were selected based on th

documents.title: A multimodal digital NeuroMarker platform with composite and domain-level validity for identification of mild cognitive impairment: a cross-sectional study.
documents.abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is a clinically heterogeneous syndrome that can represent an early manifestation of neurodegenerative disease. Diagnosis relies on assessments that are difficult to scale, leaving many individuals unidentified.

documents.title: Biosynthetic Pathways and Regulation of Antibacterial Compounds From Endophytic Fungi: From Chemistry to Genomics and Biotechnology.
documents.abstract: Endophytic fungi are non-pathogenic symbionts that represent a rich source of structurally diverse bioactive secondary metabolites. However, genome-mining studies reveal that most of their biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) remain transcriptionally silent under standard laboratory conditions, leaving much of their chemical diversity unexplored. This review examines antibacterial natural products from endophytic fungi by integrating three complementary aspects: metabolite chemistry, biosynthetic pathways, and strategies for activating cryptic BGCs. Endophytic fungi produce polyketides, non-ribos

documents.title: Interpretable Drug-Target Prediction via Geometric Alignment: A Linear Alternative to Deep Architectural Complexity.
documents.abstract: Designing selective kinase inhibitors is a multiobjective optimization problem constrained by the structural conservation of the human kinome, along with the lack of high-quality interaction data. Traditional deep learning methods often train complex neural networks directly on small datasets and fail to generalize to new chemical scaffolds. To this end, we present Geometric Manifold Alignment, a novel linear approach that shifts away from architectural complexity. We introduce Multi-View Linear Manifold (MVLM), which aligns the latent spaces of ChemBERTa (small molecules) and ESM-2 (protein s

documents.title: AI-Enabled Animal Behavior Analysis for Translational Pharmacology and Therapeutic Discovery.
documents.abstract: Animal behavior is a critical endpoint in preclinical pharmacology, toxicology, and therapeutic discovery, yet conventional behavioral scoring remains labor-intensive, low-dimensional, and difficult to reproduce across laboratories. Artificial intelligence (AI) can now quantify behavior from video with greater spatial, temporal, and phenotypic resolution. This review summarizes how object detection, markerless pose estimation, unsupervised behavioral segmentation, foundation models, and autonomous analysis agents are reshaping behavioral phenotyping. General-purpose object detectors rapidly lo

documents.title: UPLC-MS/MS-GNPS based metabolite profiling and inhibitory potential of Vitex negundo L. leaves against Shiga toxins: Applications for biodegradable films with antibacterial properties.
documents.abstract: Antibiotic therapy for STEC O157:H7 infections induces Shiga toxin release, highlighting the need for alternative, food-compatible antimicrobial strategies. The ethanolic leaf extract of Vitex negundo L. was characterized by UPLC-qTOF-MS/MS, integrated with Feature-Based Molecular Networking (GNPS), which putatively annotated 56 metabolites. Computational screening of all annotated compounds against the Stx1 and Stx2 B-subunits identified compound 8, an iridoid glycoside, as the top-ranked candidate with predicted Stx1-binding potential (ΔG = -6.9 kcal/mol; Ki = 8.7 µM). Over 100 ns of molecul

documents.title: SLC5A12 defines an invasive epithelial state associated with immune remodeling and therapeutic vulnerability in HNSCC.
documents.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is characterized by marked epithelial and immune heterogeneity. The malignant epithelial states associated with tumor progression, immune remodeling, and potential therapeutic vulnerability remain incompletely defined.
documents.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

documents.title: Design and validation of nucleosome binding peptides using BindCraft.
documents.abstract: Chromatin is a sophisticated assembly of DNA, RNA and proteins in the nuclei of eukaryotic cells. Protein-protein interactions that govern chromatin function are key regulators of genome activity, making them prime targets for drug discovery. Engineering and modulating these contacts presents a viable pathway for innovative epigenetic therapies. Nucleosomes, the primary structural units of chromatin, feature various interaction interfaces, most notably the acidic patch. This region serves as a critical binding site for numerous chromatin-associated proteins, often via their intrinsically disor

documents.title: Integrative Single-Cell and Bulk RNA Sequencing Analysis Identifies Ion Channel-Related Biomarkers in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
documents.abstract: Human ion channel genes (HICGs), as core effectors of transmembrane signal transduction, play a critical role in the initiation and progression of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, the underlying mechanisms remain largely unclear. This study aimed to investigate the potential value of ion channel genes in COPD.
documents.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

documents.title: Bone morphogenetic protein 4 meets artificial intelligence: a comprehensive review of AI-driven advances in drug discovery, structural modeling, and clinical translation.
documents.abstract: Bone Morphogenetic Protein 4 (BMP4), a member of the transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) superfamily, plays pivotal roles in embryonic development, tissue homeostasis, and disease pathogenesis-including cancer, fibrosis, and fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methodologies over the past 5 years has created unprecedented opportunities for understanding and therapeutically targeting BMP4 biology at multiple scales, from atomic-resolution structure prediction to population-level clinical prognostication.

documents.title: Hupehenine suppresses tumor cell phenotypes and modulates macrophage marker profiles in a diabeticmimetic colorectal cancer model.
documents.abstract: Diabetes is associated with increased colorectal cancer (CRC) risk and mortality, but the molecular links remain incompletely understood. We aimed to characterize shared molecular features of diabetes and CRC, and identify compounds capable of modulating the candidate axis at this interface.

documents.title: Virology-aware artificial intelligence for respiratory antiviral discovery: from molecular docking biases to RdRp-centered benchmarking.
documents.abstract: Respiratory RNA viruses remain a persistent threat because they combine high transmissibility, rapid evolution, immune escape, zoonotic spillover, and incomplete therapeutic coverage. RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (RdRps) and polymerase complexes are among the most conserved and pharmacologically actionable viral targets, yet they are also challenging computational targets because their ligandable states depend on RNA templates, cofactors, divalent metals, multidomain architecture, and conformational transitions. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), geometri

documents.title: Research progress on the application of multi-scale computational methods in the research and development of anti-tuberculosis infection drugs.
documents.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), driven by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains a leading cause of mortality from infectious disease worldwide.​ The global dissemination of multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) strains-coupled with protracted treatment regimens and the persistence of latent infection-has not only compromised first-line chemotherapies but also underscored the stagnation of conventional drug development pipelines. In this review, we systematically synthesize how multi-scale computational strategies are reshaping anti-TB drug discovery and explicitly delineate the

documents.title: Integrative transcriptomic and computational analysis associates Ms4a6c+ macrophages with fibrosis in radiation proctitis and computationally nominates MOTS-c as a candidate modulator.
documents.abstract: Chronic radiation proctitis (CRP) represents a significant clinical challenge characterized by irreversible fibrosis and a lack of specific pharmacological interventions. This study aimed to elucidate the cellular mechanisms underlying impaired tissue repair to identify novel therapeutic targets.

documents.title: Artificial intelligence and anti-cancer drugs: advancing discovery, personalization, and precision oncology.
documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the way we discover anticancer drugs. It tackles the problems of traditional methods, such as prolonged timelines for drug development, higher costs, and substantial inter-patient heterogeneity. This review explains how AI is applied throughout the cancer drug pipeline. This includes target identification, virtual screening of compounds, molecular docking, and predicting pharmacokinetics. We explore how machine learning models speed up hit-to-lead optimization, improve clinical trial design by stratifying patients, and allow for real-time toxicity monit

documents.title: Cytochrome P450 inhibitors: friends or foes?
documents.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP450) enzymes play a central role in the metabolism of xenobiotics and endogenous compounds, influencing drug pharmacokinetics, efficacy, and safety. Inhibition of these enzymes has traditionally been viewed as a major liability in drug discovery due to its association with drug-drug interactions (DDIs), toxicity, and metabolic instability. However, inhibition of specific CYP450 isoforms has emerged as a powerful therapeutic strategy in multiple disease areas, including cancer and infectious diseases. This review presents a comprehensive analysis of data and regulatory guida

documents.title: Exploration or exploitation? The double-edged effects of AI use modes on radical creativity: evidence from AI-enabled drug discovery.
documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely adopted in corporate innovation activities, yet prior research has not reached a consensus on whether it is more conducive to incremental or radical innovation. For radical innovation, which depends on highly novel ideas, realizing the value of AI depends not only on whether AI is adopted but, more importantly, on whether employees can use it creatively to transcend established knowledge boundaries. Drawing on environmental dynamism and the exploration-exploitation perspective, this study develops a theoretical model linking leaders' perceptions of

documents.title: Comparative multi-target computational profiling of ebelin lactone across cognition-associated proteins.
documents.abstract: Ebelin lactone (EL) is a bacoside-related triterpenoid derivative produced through acid hydrolysis and has previously shown binding affinity toward the M1 muscarinic and 5-HT2A receptors. However, its structural compatibility with proteins involved in synaptic plasticity, neuronal proteostasis, mitochondrial stress responses, and neurite remodeling has not been systematically evaluated.

documents.title: Mapping the subcellular pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic landscape: a systems-pharmacology framework for predicting combination therapies against intracellular bacterial infections.
documents.abstract: Intracellular bacterial pathogens represent one of the most formidable challenges in contemporary medicine. By exploiting host cellular niches, these organisms evade immune surveillance and withstand conventional antibiotic therapies, establishing persistent reservoirs that are difficult to eradicate. Although antibiotic combinations, host-directed interventions, and drug repurposing have shown promise, conventional discovery pipelines rarely capture the dynamic and compartmentalized nature of the intracellular environment. This review proposes a systems pharmacology framework centered on subc

documents.title: SCOPE-based target and pathway enrichment identifies the histamine H1 receptor as a regulator of exodosis.
documents.abstract: Phenotypic screening enables discovery of small molecules without requiring predefined targets, but mechanistic interpretation remains challenging due to polypharmacology and pathway complexity.

documents.title: Integrated in vitro and in silico assessment of antimicrobial, chemical antioxidant, and cytotoxic activities of endophytic Aspergillus sp. GK1 isolated from Mentha spicata roots.
documents.abstract: Medicinal plants are a source of structurally diverse endophytic fungi which harbor significant pharmaceutical potential.

documents.title: An m5C-associated NSUN5-YBX1-CENPF programme marks melanoma cell states and immune features.
documents.abstract: RNA 5-methylcytosine (m5C)-associated programmes may help characterise melanoma cell states and their immune context. We investigated an NSUN5-YBX1-CENPF (NYC) programme using patient-matched sequencing, experimental perturbation and multiscale transcriptomic analyses.

documents.title: Plasmid-Mediated AmpC Detection in Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae: In Vitro Prevalence and In Silico Inhibitor Design.
documents.abstract: This study investigated the prevalence of AmpC beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae in clinical specimens collected in Lahore, Pakistan, and aimed to identify potential inhibitors targeting AmpC beta-lactamases.
documents.journal: The Canadian journal of infectious diseases & medical microbiology = Journal canadien des maladies infectieuses et de la microbiologie medicale
